failure_summary: Every fault is model-side on a production-fidelity gpt-5.4-mini run (so prompt_confusion cannot be separated from model capability here): run 1 emitted an unoffered [term:centrality] slug (render_decision.zones.terms offers only double_threat) and omitted the sole requiredSet handle opp-future-fork (spec future:windows:c5r4,c7r3), leaving "their four-in-a-row line" pointing at nothing, while run 0 coined the engine-search phrase "the reply tree is looser" as a prose echo of replyHistogram, which the assembled prompt never contains (PROMPT.includes("tree") === false) and which prompt line 68 explicitly forbids.
notes: n_runs is 2 (run_index 0..1), not 5 — no sub-sampling was needed: A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 were graded on BOTH runs, so no axis is null. A5 run 0: served prose says "the reply tree is looser" — engine/game-tree terminology and a prose echo of replyHistogram; the render never supplies it (grep of the assembled prompt: "tree" absent, and the reading key at line 68 bans repeating the field/"histogram"), so the model introduced it -> prompt_confusion, not render_bug. A7b run 1: "the cleaner path to build their four-in-a-row line" is a specific-sounding referent with no named cell and no emitted [zone:...]; the fork cells c5r4/c7r3 were offered (alias opp-future-fork, truthBoard projectedDeep) and were in requiredSet, so the referent was available and dropped. G7 run 1: grade_mechanical G7b_offered=fail (unoffered term slug "centrality"); annotationRepairs is [] on both runs, so no G7c auto-fail; run 0 judgment half passes — better-col wraps "Column 4", played-col wraps "Column 3", opp-future-fork wraps "the two finishing squares they can aim at later" (two-square words on a two-square handle, future tense as the role demands), nothing over-wrapped. G1 run 1: the answer never touches the required rendered region at all. Board checks: decision board 32655 (Gray to move) scr col4=-2 vs col3=-3, i.e. lose_to_faster_lose confirmed and column 4 is genuinely the more central/more resilient square (openingContext.centralityComparison betterCell c4r2 vs playedCell c3r2, centralityGrounded true) -> A3 pass both runs. G4/G5: on render_decision.finalMovestring 32655232205200200033311111134455564, visualize_board shows major threats col5 row4 (X) [GT] and col7 row3 (X) [GT] with the c5r4/c7r3 double — every rendered threat-list entry on projectedDeepOpp and on the lostResource line 32655311113221122233355556666600 (col1 row3 X GT, col5 r2/r3/r4/r5) is board-true, and run 0 names no cell outside that line. G6: patternOnAfterBestBoard is null and the after-best board 326553 has no major threats, so the L7/sign routing is correct. G3: the only shown:false boards are afterBest/afterPlayed (tag-set identical to decision); neither answer needed them. G2: the L7 guardrail is honored on both runs — no defeatist clause, no claim the better move wins, opening/centrality framing, and run 0 states the fork matters LATER as the guardrail demands; A5b (player 2 + opening) passes on both runs. Caveat on Step 0b: this is the 2026-08-06 run, and the prompt rebuilt today with current renderReasonModel.mjs offers 10 zone aliases and a 3-handle required set, whereas the contemporaneous render_decision records 3 aliases and a 1-handle required set; per Step 0 I treated render_decision as authoritative for the offered/required sets (that is also what grade_mechanical.mjs used), and used the rebuilt prompt only for the model-independent "was this word ever shown" checks.
